title: The Margrave's Proposal
dialogue: Lucan Vael arrives with a leather portfolio and a smile that has been calibrated for this exact room.
monologue: He prepared for this meeting. The portfolio is for show — men like Vael have the numbers memorized. The portfolio is for me, so I have something to look at while he talks.

narrative.text: Chancellor. I will be brief. Veltrian Steel's northern mills are operating at sixty percent capacity. The reason is not demand — demand is strong. The reason is a regulatory framework from 1951 that was designed to protect Halvek's cronies from competition. Modernize the framework, and I can bring those mills to full capacity within eighteen months. That is four thousand jobs and a measurable GDP contribution. All I need is regulatory access.
I am not asking for a subsidy. I am asking for a fair environment. That is all.

vael_proposal.monologue: Regulatory access. He makes it sound like opening a window. Regulatory access is the door to everything else — procurement preferences, inspection schedules, licensing approvals. He is asking for the key to the house and calling it fresh air.

choices.text: "Send the specific regulations you want reviewed to Elara Vostane. She will assess them on the merits."
"Regulatory reform goes through the standard parliamentary process. I am not in the business of bespoke frameworks for private interests."
